angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 6,186,164 km at 32.53 pc = 2.54 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112748: distance 32.531 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.009), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 32.531 +/- 0.293 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 28.9340 +/- 0.1887 mas (same row, RUWE 2.89), 153.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 8.892 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112748: radius 8.892 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 44.58 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.051) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 6,186,164 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5005 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112748: effective temperature 5005 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.083) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112748: effective temperature 5005 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.083) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
